subject: math
title: Grade 4 Rounding and Estimating
seo_title: Grade 4 Rounding and Estimating Worksheets: Free Math with Answer Key (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Round whole numbers to the nearest ten, hundred, or thousand, in various contexts
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 math worksheets on rounding and estimating, aligned to the Ontario curriculum (B1.3, B1.8): round to the nearest ten, hundred and thousand, round tenths to the nearest whole number, estimate sums and differences, check if answers are reasonable and solve word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Look one place to the right: 5 or more rounds up, 4 or less rounds down. 4500 rounds to 5000 and 3.5 rounds to 4.
key_sub: Estimate before you calculate: 4682 + 2371 is about 5000 + 2000 = 7000. If your answer is far from the estimate, check your work.
body_html:
Rounding: find the closer ten, hundred or thousand

Rounding finds the closest ten, hundred or thousand. Rounded numbers are easy to add and subtract in your head.

The 5 rule

Look at the digit one place to the right of the place you are rounding to. 5 or more: round up. 4 or less: round down. Exactly halfway rounds up.

Round to the nearestLook at theExample
tenones digit2875 → 2880
hundredtens digit4519 → 4500
thousandhundreds digit7391 → 7000
whole numbertenths digit6.8 → 7
Exactly halfway

Round 4500 to the nearest thousand.

4500 is exactly halfway between 4000 and 5000. The hundreds digit is 5, and 5 rounds up.

Answer: 5000

A 9 that rounds up

Round 9615 to the nearest thousand.

The hundreds digit is 6, so round up. 9 thousands and 1 more thousand make 10 thousands.

Answer: 10 000

Round tenths to the nearest whole number

A decimal like 3.5 is between two whole numbers, 3 and 4. Look at the tenths digit.

Round a decimal

A pumpkin has a mass of 4.6 kg. What is its mass to the nearest kilogram?

The tenths digit is 6. 6 is 5 or more, so round up.

Answer: 5 kg

Estimate, then check

An estimate is a quick answer that is close to the exact answer. Round the numbers, then add or subtract in your head. If your exact answer is far from the estimate, check your work.

Estimate a sum

Estimate 4682 + 2371 to the nearest thousand.

5000 + 2000 = 7000. The exact answer is 7053, which is close.

Answer: about 7000

Is the answer reasonable?

Arjun says 5203 − 1867 = 4664.

Estimate: 5200 − 1900 = 3300. 4664 is far from 3300, so it is not reasonable. The exact answer is 3336.

Answer: not reasonable

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Rounding 4500 down to 4000Exactly halfway rounds up: 5000
Rounding the wrong place: 6382 to the nearest thousand → 6400For the nearest thousand, look at the hundreds digit: 3, so 6000
Rounding in steps: 3462 → 3500 → 4000Look only at the hundreds digit: 4, so 3000
Dropping the decimal: 3.8 → 3The tenths digit is 8 (5 or more), so 3.8 rounds to 4
Not checking: 3467 + 258 = 6047Estimate 3500 + 300 = 3800; 6047 is far too big. The answer is 3725

faq.q: What does Grade 4 learn about rounding in the Ontario math curriculum?
faq.a: Grade 4 students round whole numbers to the nearest ten, hundred or thousand in real situations (B1.3). They also round decimal tenths to the nearest whole number, such as 3.5 to 4 (B1.8).
To the nearest thousand, 4500 rounds to 5000. A number exactly halfway between two thousands is rounded up.

faq.q: How do you round a decimal to the nearest whole number?
faq.a: Look at the tenths digit. If it is 5 or more, round up; if it is 4 or less, keep the whole number. So 6.8 rounds to 7 and 7.4 rounds to 7.

faq.q: How can my child check if an answer is reasonable?
faq.a: Estimate first by rounding, then compare. If 3467 + 258 gives 6047 but 3500 + 300 = 3800, the answer is far too big and should be checked.

items.q: Round 368 to the nearest ten.
items.e: 368 is between 360 and 370. Look at the ones digit: 8. 8 is 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 370.

items.q: Round 1243 to the nearest ten.
items.e: 1243 is between 1240 and 1250. Look at the ones digit: 3. 3 is 4 or less, so round down. Answer: 1240.

items.q: Round 2875 to the nearest ten.

items.q: Round 5098 to the nearest ten.

items.q: Round 7996 to the nearest ten.
items.e: 7996 is between 7990 and 8000. Look at the ones digit: 6. 6 is 5 or more, so round up. 799 tens and 1 more ten make 800 tens, which is 8000. Answer: 8000.

items.q: Round 6431 to the nearest ten.

items.q: Which number rounds to 2470 when you round to the nearest ten?
items.e: Round each number to the nearest ten: 2466 → 2470; 2475 → 2480; 2464 → 2460; 2476 → 2480. Only 2466 rounds to 2470.

items.e: 5961 is between 5900 and 6000. Look at the tens digit: 6. 6 is 5 or more, so round up. 59 hundreds and 1 more hundred make 60 hundreds, which is 6000. Answer: 6000.

items.q: Which number rounds to 3500 when you round to the nearest hundred?

items.q: Round 9615 to the nearest thousand.
items.e: 9615 is between 9000 and 10 000. Look at the hundreds digit: 6. 6 is 5 or more, so round up. 9 thousands and 1 more thousand make 10 thousands, which is 10 000. Answer: 10 000.

items.q: Which number rounds to 3000 when you round to the nearest thousand?
items.e: Round each number to the nearest thousand: 2614 → 3000; 2499 → 2000; 3500 → 4000; 3714 → 4000. Only 2614 rounds to 3000.

items.q: Which number rounds to 7000 when you round to the nearest thousand?
items.e: Round each number to the nearest thousand: 7381 → 7000; 6499 → 6000; 7500 → 8000; 7612 → 8000. Only 7381 rounds to 7000.

items.q: What is the smallest whole number that rounds to 6000 when you round to the nearest thousand?
items.e: The numbers from 5500 to 6499 round to 6000. 5499 has a 4 in the hundreds place, so it rounds down to 5000. The smallest is 5500, because 5 in the hundreds place rounds up.

items.q: What is the largest whole number that rounds to 4000 when you round to the nearest thousand?
items.e: The numbers from 3500 to 4499 round to 4000. 4500 is exactly halfway, so it rounds up to 5000. 4490 rounds to 4000 too, but 4499 is larger. The largest is 4499.

items.q: Which digit do you look at to round 5273 to the nearest thousand?
items.e: To round to the nearest thousand, look one place to the right of the thousands: the hundreds digit, 2. 2 is 4 or less, so 5273 rounds down to 5000.

items.q: Liam says 4500 rounds to 4000 when you round to the nearest thousand. Is he right?
items.e: 4500 is exactly halfway between 4000 and 5000. The hundreds digit is 5, and 5 rounds up. Liam is not right: 4500 rounds to 5000.

items.q: Owen rounds 6382 to the nearest thousand and gets 6400. What should he get?
items.e: Owen rounded to the nearest hundred. For the nearest thousand, look at the hundreds digit: 3. 3 is 4 or less, so round down. 6382 rounds to 6000.

items.q: Maya rounds 3462 to the nearest thousand. She says “3462 → 3460 → 3500 → 4000.” What is the right answer?
items.e: Do not round in steps. To round to the nearest thousand, look only at the hundreds digit: 4. 4 is 4 or less, so round down. 3462 rounds to 3000.

sets.title: Round tenths to the nearest whole number

items.q: Round 2.3 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: 2.3 is between 2 and 3. Look at the tenths digit: 3. 3 is 4 or less, so round down. Answer: 2.

items.q: Round 6.8 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: 6.8 is between 6 and 7. Look at the tenths digit: 8. 8 is 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 7.

items.q: Round 3.5 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: 3.5 is exactly halfway between 3 and 4. The tenths digit is 5, and 5 rounds up. Answer: 4.

items.q: Round 7.4 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: 7.4 is between 7 and 8. Look at the tenths digit: 4. 4 is 4 or less, so round down. Answer: 7.

items.e: 1.6 is between 1 and 2. Look at the tenths digit: 6. 6 is 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 2.

items.q: Round 4.5 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: 4.5 is exactly halfway between 4 and 5. The tenths digit is 5, and 5 rounds up. Answer: 5.

items.q: Round 9.2 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: 9.2 is between 9 and 10. Look at the tenths digit: 2. 2 is 4 or less, so round down. Answer: 9.

items.q: Round 8.5 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: 8.5 is exactly halfway between 8 and 9. The tenths digit is 5, and 5 rounds up. Answer: 9.

items.q: Round 0.6 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: 0.6 is between 0 and 1. Look at the tenths digit: 6. 6 is 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 1.

items.e: 12.4 is between 12 and 13. Look at the tenths digit: 4. 4 is 4 or less, so round down. Answer: 12.

items.q: Round 9.7 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: 9.7 is between 9 and 10. Look at the tenths digit: 7. 7 is 5 or more, so round up. 9 + 1 = 10. Answer: 10.

items.q: A pumpkin from the farm has a mass of 4.6 kg. What is its mass to the nearest kilogram?
items.e: 4.6 is between 4 and 5. Look at the tenths digit: 6. 6 is 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 5 kg.

items.q: Kai skis a trail that is 3.4 km long. How long is the trail to the nearest kilometre?
items.e: 3.4 is between 3 and 4. Look at the tenths digit: 4. 4 is 4 or less, so round down. Answer: 3 km.

items.q: Ethan’s water jug holds 1.5 L. How much does it hold to the nearest litre?
items.e: 1.5 is exactly halfway between 1 and 2. The tenths digit is 5, and 5 rounds up. Answer: 2 L.

items.q: Sofia cuts a piece of ribbon 6.5 m long for a craft. How long is it to the nearest metre?
items.e: 6.5 is exactly halfway between 6 and 7. The tenths digit is 5, and 5 rounds up. Answer: 7 m.

items.q: On a snow day, 14.3 cm of snow falls in Ottawa. How much snow is that to the nearest centimetre?
items.e: 14.3 is between 14 and 15. Look at the tenths digit: 3. 3 is 4 or less, so round down. Answer: 14 cm.

items.q: Hana’s family drives 19.8 km to the skating rink. How far is that to the nearest kilometre?
items.e: 19.8 is between 19 and 20. Look at the tenths digit: 8. 8 is 5 or more, so round up. 19 + 1 = 20. Answer: 20 km.

items.q: Which decimal rounds to 5 when you round to the nearest whole number?
items.e: Round each one: 4.6 → 5; 4.4 → 4; 5.5 → 6; 5.6 → 6. Only 4.6 rounds to 5.

items.q: Zoe says 6.5 rounds to 6 when you round to the nearest whole number. Is she right?
items.e: 6.5 is exactly halfway between 6 and 7. The tenths digit is 5, and 5 rounds up. Zoe is not right: 6.5 rounds to 7.

items.q: Nathan rounds 3.8 to the nearest whole number. He drops the .8 and gets 3. What should he get?
items.e: Look at the tenths digit: 8. 8 is 5 or more, so round up. 3.8 is closer to 4 than to 3. Answer: 4.

items.q: Mateo’s family drives 448 km from Toronto to Ottawa, then 198 km from Ottawa to Montréal. About how far do they drive? Round to the nearest ten.
items.e: Round to the nearest ten: 450 km + 200 km = 650 km. (The exact answer is 646 km.)

items.q: A maple syrup farm makes 1265 L of syrup in March and 842 L in April. About how much syrup is that? Round to the nearest hundred.
items.e: Round to the nearest hundred: 1300 L + 800 L = 2100 L. (The exact answer is 2107 L.)

items.q: The school raises $2385 at the Terry Fox Run this year and $2940 last year. About how much is that in all? Round to the nearest hundred.
items.e: Round to the nearest hundred: $2400 + $2900 = $5300. (The exact answer is $5325.)

items.q: 3478 fans watch a hockey game on Friday and 2856 fans watch on Saturday. About how many more fans come on Friday? Round to the nearest hundred.
items.e: Round to the nearest hundred: 3500 − 2900 = 600. (The exact answer is 622.)

items.q: Bird watchers count 2650 Canada geese on Monday and 3180 on Tuesday. About how many geese is that? Round to the nearest thousand.
items.e: Round to the nearest thousand: 3000 + 3000 = 6000. (The exact answer is 5830.)

items.q: Owen’s backpack has a mass of 3.6 kg. His lunch bag has a mass of 1.3 kg. About what is the total mass? Round each to the nearest whole number.
items.e: Round each number to the nearest whole number: 4 kg + 1 kg = 5 kg. (The exact answer is 4.9 kg.)

items.q: On a canoe trip, Priya’s group paddles 6.4 km before lunch and 4.5 km after lunch. About how far do they paddle? Round each to the nearest whole number.
items.e: Round each number to the nearest whole number: 6 km + 5 km = 11 km. (The exact answer is 10.9 km.)

items.q: Chloe has 8.7 m of ribbon. She uses 2.4 m for a gift. About how much ribbon is left? Round each to the nearest whole number.
items.e: Round each number to the nearest whole number: 9 m − 2 m = 7 m. (The exact answer is 6.3 m.)

items.q: Ava works out 2385 + 1476 and gets 3861. Is the answer reasonable? Round to the nearest hundred to check.
items.e: Estimate: 2400 + 1500 = 3900. 3861 is close to 3900, so it is reasonable.

items.q: Arjun works out 5203 − 1867 and gets 4664. Is the answer reasonable? Round to the nearest hundred to check.
items.e: Estimate: 5200 − 1900 = 3300. 4664 is far from 3300, so it is not reasonable. The exact answer is 3336. (The smaller digit was taken from the bigger digit in each column. Regroup instead: you cannot take 7 from 3.)

items.q: Leah works out 3467 + 258 and gets 6047. Is the answer reasonable? Round to the nearest hundred to check.
items.e: Estimate: 3500 + 300 = 3800. 6047 is far from 3800, so it is not reasonable. The exact answer is 3725. (258 was lined up under the wrong places, as if it were 2580. Line up ones with ones.)

items.q: Benjamin works out 7020 − 3984 and gets 3036. Is the answer reasonable? Round to the nearest thousand to check.
items.e: Estimate: 7000 − 4000 = 3000. 3036 is close to 3000, so it is reasonable.

items.q: A sugar bush sells 1680 bottles of syrup in spring and 2790 bottles in fall. Mei estimates 2000 + 3000 = 5000 bottles. Did it sell more or less than 5000 bottles?
c: Less, both numbers were rounded up
More, both numbers were rounded up
More, both numbers were rounded down
Less, both numbers were rounded down
items.e: 1680 → 2000 and 2790 → 3000. Both numbers were rounded up, so 5000 is too big. The exact total is 4470 bottles, which is less than 5000.

items.q: Jayden’s school wants to read 6000 pages in October. Grade 4 reads 4180 pages and Grade 5 reads 2345 pages. Jayden estimates 4000 + 2000 = 6000. Did they read more or less than 6000 pages?
c: More, both numbers were rounded up
More, both numbers were rounded down
Less, both numbers were rounded up
Less, both numbers were rounded down
items.e: 4180 → 4000 and 2345 → 2000. Both numbers were rounded down, so 6000 is too small. The exact total is 6525 pages, which is more than 6000.

items.q: The arena has 6000 seats. 3420 adults and 2190 children have tickets for a hockey game. Are there enough seats? Round to the nearest hundred to decide.
items.e: Round to the nearest hundred: 3400 + 2200 = 5600. 5600 is less than 6000, so yes. (The exact answer is 5610.)

items.q: Hana’s family has $1500 for a trip to Halifax. The hotel costs $865 and gas and food cost $712. Is $1500 enough? Round to the nearest hundred to decide.
items.e: Round to the nearest hundred: $900 + $700 = $1600. $1600 is more than $1500, so no. (The exact answer is $1577.)

items.q: A fall fair sells 2465 tickets on Saturday, 1830 on Sunday and 1275 on Monday. About how many tickets is that? Round to the nearest hundred.
items.e: Round to the nearest hundred: 2500 + 1800 + 1300 = 5600. (The exact answer is 5570.)

items.q: The goal for the food drive is 5000 cans. The students have 3260 cans. About how many more cans do they need? Round to the nearest hundred.
items.e: Round to the nearest hundred: 5000 − 3300 = 1700. (The exact answer is 1740.)
